messages:
rachael: quick notesupport ticket shows customers copy/pasting our retry examples and getting immediate 429s. opening a coordination thread to make a tiny docs patch.
devin: can you paste the failing response blob?
sam: got it from the customer logs:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 7
{"error":"rate_limited"}
```
sam: two obvious problems: the JS snippet still references `maxRetries` (SDK now accepts `retryCount`) and our prose suggests a fixed 1s sleep. that makes things worse when Retry-After is provided.
hao: agreed. proposal: (1) add a compact migration table (old -> new keys), (2) swap fixed sleep for a tiny language-agnostic backoff pattern with jitter, (3) call out honoring Retry-After and (4) add one-line stream guidance for partial payloads/timeouts. keep it short.
rachael: for migration table include `maxRetries -> retryCount`, `timeoutMs -> requestTimeout`, `contextWindow -> maxContextTokens`. customers keep pasting the deprecated names.
devin: suggestion for the backoff note: show a small Go example (we have lots of Python/JS already). keep it tiny:
```go
func retryWithBackoff(op func() error, retries int) error {
  for i := 0; i < retries; i++ {
    if err := op(); err != nil {
      if i == retries-1 { return err }
      // exponential base 200ms + jitter up to 100ms
      delay := time.Duration((1<<uint(i))*200+rand.Intn(100)) * time.Millisecond
      time.Sleep(delay)
      continue
    }
    return nil
  }
  return nil
}
```
sam: nice. also add a note: "If the server returns Retry-After, delay at least that many seconds before retrying." put that before the codeblock.
hao: add a short troubleshooting checklist at the top of the page: "If you observe repeated 429s: 1) Confirm SDK keys (see migration table); 2) Respect Retry-After header; 3) Use exponential backoff + jitter; 4) For streams: handle partial messages and log aborted streams."
rachael: also add a tiny grep pattern to help support triage: `stream aborted: requestTimeout=\d+ms` so support can quickly search customer logs. keep it one line.
devin: docs-ci: I will open a focused PR that only replaces the fixed-sleep snippet, inserts the migration table, adds the Go helper and the checklist, and updates the link to the SDK changelog. small atomic change.
sam: make sure to include a one-line changelog blurb so SDK release notes can link back. don't duplicate SDK wording.
